study type: Retrospective cohort study for machine learning model development and validation
exposure: Patient characteristics used as features in machine learning models
outcome: Successful vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC)
cohort: A total of 2438 pregnant women with trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) and one prior cesarean section, from two tertiary hospitals in Guangdong province of China.
finding: The CatBoost machine learning model demonstrated the best performance (AUC 0.767) in predicting successful VBAC, with cervical Bishop score and interpregnancy interval showing the greatest impact.
mod_finding: The study developed an explainable machine learning model to predict successful vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC), identifying cervical Bishop score and interpregnancy interval as key predictive factors.
